page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-912 is a high-capacity, general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Driven by AMD EPYC 7742 processors operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz, this instance provisions 114 dedicated physical cores supporting 2 threads per core, delivering a total of 228 vCPUs. The compute capacity is paired with 912.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance configuration features no bundled local storage, requiring persistent storage needs to be addressed through attached network block volumes. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and features zero hardware accelerators or GPUs. From an infrastructure cost perspective, this flexible shape provides high resource consolidation density on dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources, offering favorable qualitative cost efficiency for organizations looking to aggregate massive multi-threaded parallel workloads without the overhead of physical host management.

The primary tradeoff of the VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-912 lies in its lack of native ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies heavily on external storage network throughput. The architecture is best matched for enterprise-grade general-purpose workloads requiring significant thread concurrency and memory scale, including massive in-memory batch processing, distributed enterprise applications, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and container orchestration nodes.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E3.Flex.114-912 is a large-scale general-purpose virtual machine designed for dense multi-threaded compute workloads. Powered by AMD EPYC 7742 processors clocked at 2.25 GHz, this instance features 114 dedicated physical cores (228 vCPUs via multithreading) and 912.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating external network-attached volumes for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By offering dedicated CPU allocation at massive scale, the platform provides substantial throughput for thread-intensive enterprise workloads while avoiding physical infrastructure management overhead. This virtual server is primarily fitted for large-scale enterprise services, multi-tenant container orchestration, large batch data pipelines, continuous integration clusters, and distributed application platforms requiring extensive core counts and memory capacity.
